title: A cotton MAPK cascade protects the cell wall against Verticillium wilt
content: Plant immunity relies on defense responses that are conserved across species and effective against diverse pathogens. Once a pathogen is perceived at the cell surface, that signal must be relayed to the nucleus to reprogram gene expression. Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascades are central to this relay: a MAPK kinase kinase (MAPKKK) phosphorylates and activates a MAPK kinase (MKK), which in turn activates a MAPK that phosphorylates downstream targets, including transcription factors.
